title: How Does a Microwave Actually Heat Food? 🔥 #shorts
description:
No flame, no hot coil. A microwave's magnetron fills the oven with 12 cm radio waves whose electric field swings 2.45 billion times a second, twisting water molecules until they heat up. Here's why the middle of your food stays cold, why the plate spins, and how the door's metal mesh keeps the waves in while you watch.

Follow Hidden Mechanics for more everyday engineering, explained in under a minute.
